newsitem.title: USA: Edison seeks federal power deregulation plan.
newsitem.headline: Edison seeks federal power deregulation plan.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co called Thursday for federal legislation to set a deadline by which time all consumers would have the right to choose their electricity supplier.

At a Senate Energy Committee workshop on the issue in Washington D.C., Edison president Stephen Frank underscored the need for a nationwide law to "complement - not undermine - state progress on competition," he said in a statement.
"Until such time as all states offer customer choice, federal legislation must include reciprocity provisions to ensure that competition occurs on a fair and symmetrical basis," Frank said.
California approved legislation last year to begin opening the state's retail electricity industry to competition in 1998.
Frank also warned that Congress needs to put all market participants in the same position relative to subsidies, tax and regulatory treatment.

He cited action by municipal utilities to link up with power marketers and marketing activity by federal agencies, such as the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) in the Pacific Northwest, as examples of unfair competition.
Frank also urged that BPA and other government-owned power marketing entities turn over control of their transmission systems to independent operators.
